summary.text: Edwin Howell "Ed" Kemon of Vergennes, a Republican, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Attorney General of Vermont to incumbent Charity Clark.
The Vermont Republican committee chose him in August 2026 after H. Brooke Paige, who had been certified the winner of the August 11 Republican primary for the office, withdrew.

paragraphs.text: Ed Kemon is 71 and lives in Vergennes.

In Vermont Public's candidate guide, where answers appear as submitted, he lists his occupation as a model-based systems engineer and also lists service as president of a Lions Club and as a Fairfax Co. election chief.

In the same guide, Kemon said the law must be enforced fairly and impartially, and he named public safety as the central issue, particularly "stopping the practice of releasing repeat offenders onto the streets without meaningful penalty."
He also said crimes against children must be a priority and that he would prioritize enforcing consumer-protection laws against frauds and scams that target older and vulnerable Vermonters.
He received 32.1% of the vote to Charity Clark's 67.7%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
